fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled XML string length plus one sizes the buffer that the parser will operate on; here the input is the 4-byte document '<a>x' so len is 5.
For len <= SMALL_XML (4096) the copy buffer is allocated with alloca(), i.e. a dynamic-stack buffer of exactly len bytes; ASan poisons it as a dynamic stack region.
Input bytes are copied in with the NUL terminator at xml[len-1]; the buffer is exactly len bytes so xml[len] is the first byte past the end.
pi.str points at xml and pi.end points at the NUL terminator (one past the last content byte); pi.s is advanced by the parser as it consumes the document.
The '<a' start tag is dispatched to read_element, which parses the element and its children.
The character after the start tag is not '<', so the content 'x' is read as element text via read_text.
read_text consumes the NUL terminator at pi->end and pi->s advances to pi->end + 1, i.e. xml + len, one byte past the dynamic-stack buffer; the safety invariant pi->s <= pi->end is violated.

fine_trace.code: case '\0': set_error(&pi->err, "invalid format, document not terminated", pi->str, pi->s); return;
fine_trace.note: The out-of-bounds pointer pi->s (xml + len) is handed to set_error as the 'current' location argument.
The backward scan dereferences *current at current == xml + len, reading one byte past the end of the alloca'd dynamic-stack buffer; ASan reports dynamic-stack-buffer-overflow READ 1.
